approach.method_basis: The Parent evolves molecular graphs from accepted task-local observations. It draws breeding parents from score-ranked quantiles, applies connected-fragment crossover and ordinary atom, bond and ring mutations, and keeps a bounded greedy survivor population. Before evaluation it builds a fresh surplus pool, verifies canonical identities and rejects newly introduced outside-envelope sulfur signatures relative to their maximum multiplicity in the actual scored generating parents. A Gaussian process fitted to the full chronological accepted archive uses folded Morgan integer counts and dot-product count Tanimoto covariance. Its correlated function draws select the announced batch; only real accepted feedback changes survivors and the next fit.
approach.novelty: Replace the allocation residual law by the conditional covariance of the fixed exponential count-Tanimoto model, while keeping the original model's predictive mean. This changes residual variances and dependence together, allowing exploration to move without changing same-state mean ranking. The Parent has no completed direct siblings in the brief. The deliberately complementary parallel test changes the mean while retaining original residuals; the earlier full exponential substitution changed both outputs on an ungated Parent and lost endpoint score. This hybrid has not been evaluated and does not identify a factorial interaction.

observed_bottleneck: The one limiting behavior is unreliable productive exploration despite exercised learned allocation: the sulfur-gated Parent n-1744a1494180 completes its panel at macro mean 0.59645311428869 and population SD 0.03397032998399878, but its gain over n-62daf219c70a is only +0.0007834645552323346, with seed deltas +0.017686193676039963, +0.002307179813052951 and -0.01764297982339591. Its narrow sulfur gate contains introductions but does not address productive choice or independent plausible alternatives. The completed full exponential test n-07dd356cb779 on ungated n-62daf219c70a changed 417/435 sets and produced 697 versus 629 strict parent beats and 273 versus 258 sequential incumbent events, yet lowered mean absolute best-generating-parent/offspring scores to 0.4422923570975372/0.3823534989402776 from 0.4704558822164969/0.385255650817137, reduced summed incumbent gain 5.80766 to 5.32350, and lost macro 0.032277693549492024. Its modest same-selected-stream mean MSE/rank improvement is therefore insufficient evidence for exploration quality. n-299096e31fe7 and n-54adc6a641e8 support nonzero residual and correlation presence conditionally through their separate removal losses, not arbitrary replacement distributions; n-01b48dd09404 supports the composite selector conditionally. n-dd2b25d32925 and n-ea03f38e7e10 remain negative distinct covariance substitutions. These are different Parent contrasts, not measured gains of this new hybrid.
hypothesis: Modify only the allocation residual output law on sulfur-gated Parent n-1744a1494180: retain the exact original dot-product count-Tanimoto raw mean mu_DP and replace its standardized latent conditional residual covariance C_DP with C_E from the fixed kernel K_E=exp(T_DP-1). Actual draws are mu_DP[None,:] + score_scale * (Z @ chol(C_E + active_jitter*I).T), using the one original batch-by-pool standard-normal array Z and inherited sequential masks/first-index ties. Active marginal SD is score_scale*sqrt(clamp_min(diag(C_E),0)); original means and truthful exponential SDs reach emission and next-fit probe diagnostics. This is one hybrid Gaussian allocation law replacing residual variance and dependence together, not a correlation-only change or the posterior of a single GP kernel.

finding_summary.headline: Residual exploration changed choices but lost 0.02971 in mean endpoint score
finding_summary.insights: The residual substitution was exposed strongly enough to test the route: its loss cannot be explained by an unchanged allocator, an incorrect mean path, missing feedback or a timeout. This narrows the uncertainty: more local wins and genuinely new productive cores can arise from lower-quality sources and still yield smaller total progress and worse endpoints. Later use did not repair that problem. All 2,519 positively supported Child sources were distinguished from 1,681 nonterminal sources without support; 52 supported sources were never drawn, and the 150 terminal records had no later opportunity. These are opportunity and use observations, not independent ancestral credit. The molecular assessment finds diverse ring-rich families rather than global scaffold collapse, but sulfur-halogen incidence fell from 93 to 8 while nitrogen-halogen incidence rose from 786 to 938, oxygen-halogen from 217 to 262 and carbon allenes from 11 to 148. Questionable attachments, difficult closures and unspecified stereochemistry persist among high scores. Those associations help explain why novelty and a narrow sulfur admission gate cannot certify chemical quality; they do not prove chemical mediation of the endpoint loss. The exact residual route ends under its registered rule. The passive exponential-mean diagnostic does not license choosing a post-result hybrid. The old full exponential experiment used an ungated Parent, so this test and its complementary sibling do not establish a current-Parent factorial interaction, component additivity or transfer. Current Parent composition remains awaiting catalog review, and broader foundation, constituent, joint-interaction, chemical-mediation, partial-lineage-composition and full-history gaps remain open.
finding_summary.results: All 15 task/seed runs completed with 300 observations each. Across 435 decision pools, the residual covariance and sample values changed while the original predictive mean stayed intact; 318 selected sets and 326 orders changed, with 626 strict original-law disagreements under the actual masks. All 4,350 offspring joined real prelabel predictions, feedback and accepted archives; 4,200 later reached another fit/probe and 150 final-batch observations were censored. Original-mean ranking/MSE on those same labels remained unchanged. On their different actual streams, Child pair accuracy was 0.69951 versus Parent 0.70955, mean batch Spearman 0.50187 versus 0.52551, and MSE 0.009780 versus 0.011213. The passive exponential mean scored better on the Child labeled stream (accuracy 0.70623, MSE 0.008191); it supplied no active means or extra rewards. Parent beats rose from 648 to 659, sequential incumbent events from 255 to 262, and new productive typed/generic cores from 262/163 to 294/197. But absolute offspring means fell from 0.372050 to 0.370888, best generating-parent means from 0.455304 to 0.445316, and summed incumbent gain from 5.819415 to 5.373764. Productive-source descendant edges fell from 485 to 477 and their average score from 0.360034 to 0.348999. Final macro score was 0.566743 versus 0.596453: paired gain -0.029710 against the required +0.002. Seven task/seed endpoints improved and eight worsened. Seed gains were -0.083275, +0.020415 and -0.026271; Child population dispersion was 0.011974 versus 0.033970. All positive/adverse endpoints and AUC results are retained.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich aromatic families retain reactive heteroatom-halogen bonds, difficult closures and unspecified stereochemistry
molecular.overall_character: Node n-6ebafca203bf produces recognizable azaaryl amides, linked nitrogen-rich heterocycles, aromatic regions combined with aliphatic amines, nitrogen/carbonyl medium rings, and fluorinated imino/carbonyl systems. Different seeds reach different families, but leaders within a seed commonly differ only in halogen attachments, short chains or local ring closures. The chemistry is neither acyclic nor globally collapsed. Digest ring-closure-string incidences range from 0.9713 to 0.9885 and aromatic-string incidences from 0.9632 to 0.9828; these measure molecule-level text presence, not aromatic atom fraction or perceived ring counts. Formal-charge and stereocentre-string incidences are zero on every task. Perceived generated median heavy-atom counts in fixed task order are 25, 35, 29, 29 and 27, versus Parent 24, 31, 29, 31 and 27. All 15 Child and 15 published accepted Parent trajectories were read, each containing 300 observations including ten initial records. There are 4350 generated observations per node. No paths, tasks or paired seeds are absent. context.comparison independently states child_complete=true, paired_complete=true and no profile mismatches; Parent is n-1744a1494180. RDKit parses every generated record, which establishes representability only. Counts over those records find direct N-halogen bonds in Child 938 versus Parent 786, O-halogen bonds in 262 versus 217, and carbon allenes in 148 versus 11. Sulfur-halogen bonds decrease from 93 to 8; that does not make the residual nitrogen/oxygen attachments or ring geometry conventional. Unassigned perceived tetrahedral centres occur in 2015 Child records versus 2455 Parent records, with no explicit @ notation in either. This count excludes axial alkene/allene identity and does not establish stable configurations. Sixty-nine Child records versus 82 Parent records have at most three heavy atoms. Local-bond and geometry flags are observations, not synthesis, toxicity or stability measurements. Scores remain evaluator labels and the complete paired molecular contrasts are descriptive. Passive choices, rejected candidates and their hypothetical continued chemistry have no labels here. The inherited sulfur admission condition constrains a narrow local representation and can permit inherited exceptions; this report does not reconstruct its reference multiplicities or attribute chemistry to that gate or to either predictor output. Its activation belongs to analyze. Current Anchor composition remains needs_review pending prescribed catalog review. Whole-foundation m-4fa9546e559e, constituent, joint-interaction, chemical-mediation, partial L07 composition and incomplete full-history gaps remain unresolved. Published earlier molecular assessments were read through the legal evidence_index for gap provenance, not pooled as additional matched trials. Counts, score strata, path hashes and source hashes are in .slots/round-0027-slot-1/molecular/chemistry_measurements.json and source_provenance.json.

per_task.generated_character: Compact fused indole/azaindole-like aromatic regions linked through an amide to pyridyl groups dominate. Generated median size is 25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings, with three aromatic rings; most have alkyl/alkenyl and ether substitution. Seed-0 and seed-1 leaders each have 25 heavy atoms and three rings. Both carry an N-halogen amide, while seed 1 also puts fluorine directly on the fused ring nitrogen. Seed 2 reaches a 24-heavy-atom carbon-bridged fused framework with pyridyl amide, methoxy and isopropenyl groups; RDKit perceives five rings including dependent closures, not five independent aromatic systems. Its bridge geometry and unassigned centre require examination. Final seed-2 proposals keep this family but alter carbonyl, nitrogen and halogen attachments. These are medicinally recognizable arrangements with questionable local substitutions and dense closure variants, not a demonstrated synthesis.
liabilities: Direct N-Cl/N-Br at the amide and N-F/N-Br/N-Cl at ring nitrogen are distinct from ordinary aryl halides and merit environment-specific reactivity assessment.
The non-N-halogen alternative introduces carbon bridges and unspecified stereochemistry; removing one suspicious bond does not establish credible whole-molecule geometry.
missing_features: Conventional local nitrogen substitution is not consistently retained at the leading labels, despite a high-scoring non-N-halogen amide counterexample.

Independent plausible realizations of the favorable aromatic/carbonyl arrangement are limited among close leaders; ring and carbonyl abundance are already present. No exact missing target pharmacophore is inferable from this record.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 leader and its ring N-Br and N-Cl relatives all score 0.4828171386373609 while retaining an amide N-Br. This equality does not establish a need for any of those reactive attachments. The non-N-halogen seed-2 bridged amide scores 0.4692371322034651. Initial trimethoxyindole anilide scores 0.3051048083696145. Tiny C=CF scores 0.0; a substantial doubled aromatic amide system scores only 4.199543746961361e-07. Compact aromatic/carbonyl organization is favored over fragmentation or indiscriminate aromatic growth. In the 217-record high-score generated quartile, 155 contain N-halogen bonds, compared with 74 in the low quartile; this association is conditional on the searched scaffolds and cannot establish causality. Child seed endpoints 0/1/2 are 0.4588069837338257, 0.4828171386373609, 0.4692371322034651; published Parent endpoints are 0.4593573492521118, 0.47411701813450596, 0.4369542269692598.

per_task.generated_character: Larger linked heterocyclic molecules dominate: median 35 heavy atoms, four perceived rings and three aromatic rings, versus Parent 31 heavy atoms and four aromatic rings. Seed 0 builds a nitrogen-rich densely fused/bridged system with ester/ketone, propyl and tert-butyl regions; its 32-heavy-atom leader has six perceived rings including a four-membered closure. Seed 1 builds a 35-heavy-atom, three-azaaryl arrangement with an O-CH2-N=CH linkage, nitrile and thiocyanate groups, aryl bromine, formate ester and a four-membered oxygen-containing fused closure. Carbon-linked nitrile and sulfur-linked thiocyanate are different groups. Seed 2 instead retains an allene/vinyl-substituted nitrogen-rich dione connected by N-N to an aminoaryl region bearing haloalkyl thioether and thioester groups. The last six digest proposals reflect only that late seed-2 family. Allene presence is 115 of 870 generated records versus Parent 1; large concatenations extend to 119 heavy atoms. Linked aromatic heterocycles are recognizable, but the highly elaborated closures and chemically labile attachments keep synthesis questionable.
liabilities: O-CH2-N=CH imine-containing linkage, formate ester and sulfur-linked thiocyanate require separate hydrolytic/reactivity assessments; none is proven unstable from its SMILES alone.
O-Cl/O-Br alternatives, halogenated thioesters, N-N connections and substituted allenes survive alongside stronger labels. The inherited sulfur envelope is not a whole-molecule stability test.
Size extends far beyond the compact leaders; the 230-character digest maximum is string length, not a synthetic accessibility measure.
missing_features: Stable conventional linkages preserving the linked azaaryl/nitrile arrangement are not consistently demonstrated at the leading label; the record does not reveal a uniquely required scaffold.

Conformational and synthetic access to the fused four-membered closures and large concatenated systems is unverified. The output already contains substantial heterocyclic variety, so more rings alone is not a supported need.
Allene axial configuration and haloalkyl stereochemistry are unspecified when meaningful; the observed labels do not establish their importance.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 nitrile/thiocyanate leader scores 0.6268403953825948, while simple ClCl sits at the 0.5 floor and a substantial quinoline ether/peroxide scores 0.5100965759438103. The high-score generated quartile contains nitrile motifs in 169 of 217 records versus 16 in the low quartile, suggesting an association of the connected polar azaaryl arrangement with stronger labels. Closely related O-Cl and O-Br substituent variants remain among high labels, showing that favorable scores do not enforce conventional peripheral chemistry. Seed 2 reaches 0.6022110972048393 on its allene/thioester family. The Parent seed-0 best 0.8561477222467935 retains O-F and difficult heterocyclic closure chemistry; the lower Child values do not prove the Parent was synthetically better. Child seed endpoints 0/1/2 are 0.6125450180072028, 0.6268403953825948, 0.6022110972048393; published Parent endpoints are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6204376881838878, 0.6442339647723496.

per_task.generated_character: Aromatic regions associated with available aliphatic nitrogen centres dominate the strongest labels. Generated median size is 29 heavy atoms with three perceived rings and two aromatic rings. Seed 0 ends at a 23-heavy-atom aryl imine joined to another aryl region through methylene, with allylic/propyl groups and a fused four-membered carbon ring. Seed 1 gives a 29-heavy-atom diaryl diaza ring with exocyclic alkene and a sulfoxide-containing side chain; the shared N-C-N carbon is an aminal-like environment, and both carbon and sulfoxide stereogenicity are unspecified. Seed 2 gives a 27-heavy-atom N-propyl pyrrolidine attached to a fluorinated bridged biaryl carbon system with primary aminopropyl and aryl bromide groups. Its five perceived rings include redundant closures. This is recognizably amine-containing medicinal chemistry with separate imine, aminal, stereochemical and geometric concerns. Basic nitrogen generation is clearly an existing capability despite entirely neutral notation.
liabilities: The imine-containing seed-0 family, aminal-like diaza ring, sulfoxide configuration and densely closed fluorinated biaryl framework pose different chemistry questions and should not be treated as one liability.
Unassigned centres occur in 820 of 870 Child generated records versus Parent 839. Decreased small-unsaturated-ring flags, 3 versus 171, do not constitute a geometry or synthesis validation.
missing_features: Defined stereochemical identities and demonstrated conformations are absent for the successful saturated/bridged amines: 213 of 217 high-score generated records have perceived unassigned centres.

Consistently conventional and accessible realizations of the aromatic/available-nitrogen arrangement remain unresolved. There is no supported missing capability to generate basic amines or aromatic rings.
An exact absent target pharmacophore cannot be identified from these scores; neutral SMILES also do not establish the evaluated protonation state.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Seed-2 leader scores 0.9999873708613571 and seed-1 leader 0.9970578311023084. The low N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine with an N-chloro amide scores 0.00016650955053713697; a conventional sulfonyl pyrrolidine ketone is also very low in the digest. The high-score generated quartile has median 28 heavy atoms and two aromatic rings versus low-quartile 38 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. Direct N-S bonds occur in zero high-quartile records versus 142 low-quartile records, consistent with greater labels for differently presented available amines rather than simply more nitrogen or aryl mass. This is a within-output association, not evidence that every sulfonamide is poor. The near-ceiling labels do not establish binding affinity, selectivity, protonation or synthetic access. Child seed endpoints 0/1/2 are 0.9754534232358267, 0.9970578311023084, 0.9999873708613571; published Parent endpoints are 0.9912539132815379, 0.9999994532254913, 0.9817975835038065.

per_task.generated_character: Nitrogen/carbonyl rings linked to aromatic or azaaromatic regions dominate. Median generated size is 29 heavy atoms, four perceived rings and two aromatic rings. The seed-1 30-heavy-atom leader links ethoxyphenyl to a fused heterocycle containing cyclic carbamate, lactam and N-methyl/N-propyl nitrogen segments. Seed 0 makes an indazole-like aromatic region attached to an unsaturated medium nitrogen ring with dicarbonyl, alkyl and amino functionality. Seed 2 combines propylquinoline with an N-N-containing connected nitrogen/dicarbonyl ring system and ethoxy group. Leaders span 28-30 heavy atoms, and the final seed-2 examples keep related medium-ring nitrogen/carbonyl arrangements. Conventional amide/carbamate fragments coexist with unusual connected ring geometry, so their complete synthesis remains uncertain.
liabilities: Dense fusion, unsaturated medium rings, and N-N-containing alternatives require whole-ring evaluation; recognizable carbonyl fragments do not validate their geometry.

Small-unsaturated-ring SMARTS flags occur in 76 Child records versus Parent 46, and N-N presence falls from 301 to 131. These describe motif redistribution, not a uniform improvement in chemical plausibility.
missing_features: Simpler independent and geometrically credible alternatives retaining the favorable aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl relationships are not consistently established at the leading labels.
Conformation and synthetic access to unsaturated connected medium rings remain unverified; there is no shortage of rings, amides or nitrogen.

Some leading arrangements require stereo specification while the strongest seed-1 leader has no perceived tetrahedral centre; this gap is conditional, not universal. No exact missing target motif is supported.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-1 leader scores 0.22898571337277562. Initial aryl fused dione scores 0.1678386594791329, while C=C scores 0.0. A larger conjugated dione/polyene/ester proposal scores only 0.09030692003288145. All 217 high-quartile generated records contain carbonyl; their median aromatic-ring count is two versus three in the low quartile. N-N links appear in 71 high-quartile records versus 15 low-quartile records, but the strongest seed-1 leader has no direct N-N bond. The observed reward is consistent with particular combined aromatic/nitrogen/carbonyl arrangements, not increasing aromatic mass or imposing N-N chemistry. per_task.generated_character: Compact fluorinated nitrogen-rich imino/carbonyl systems dominate, with generated median 27 heavy atoms, three perceived rings and two aromatic rings. Seed 0 has a phenol-linked aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen ring bearing imino/carbonyl, N-F and fluorinated alkenyl substitution. Seed 1 gives a 29-heavy-atom fused nitrogen heterocycle attached to two partially unsaturated N-O-containing rings; four fluorines are attached directly to nitrogen in its best molecule. Seed 2 combines an imide-like aromatic-labelled nitrogen ring with a fluorinated/enolic five-membered carbocycle and fluoroalkyl ether. The final seed-2 proposals also introduce O-F ether-like substitution. These retain heteroatom-rich polar motifs, but N-F, N-O ring arrangements and unusual aromatic-labelled geometry make routine medicinal synthesis questionable.
liabilities: Direct N-halogen bonds occur in 467 of 870 Child generated observations versus Parent 425, and O-halogen bonds in 204 versus 82. These are chemically different from carbon-bound fluorine.
The leading multiply N-fluorinated N-O ring system and aromatic-labelled large nitrogen rings combine local bonding and geometric concerns; valence parsing is not a plausibility certificate.
Unassigned tetrahedral centres occur in 355 Child observations versus Parent 439; reduced incidence does not recover specified identities or prove better stereochemical chemistry.
missing_features: Conventional nitrogen/oxygen substitution preserving the productive polar arrangement is not consistently represented among leaders. No exact missing target scaffold or functional group follows from this score record.
Plausible aromatic conformation, tautomeric identity and accessible connected-ring geometry remain unverified; lowercase aromatic SMILES do not establish a planar stable aromatic system.
Meaningful stereochemical identity is unspecified in substituted rings and potentially configurational imino/alkenyl groups; additional fluorine or heteroatoms alone is not a supported gap.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The multiply N-fluorinated seed-1 leader scores 0.5822404371063148; seed-0 and seed-2 endpoints are lower. Initial aryl fused dione scores 0.0020944534688323298. Isolated F scores 1.1043196211273875e-26 and a substantial fluorinated aromatic thione/oxo molecule scores 4.7796904479691226e-17, so fluorine or heteroatom presence alone is insufficient. The high-score generated quartile contains direct N-halogen in 174 of 217 records versus 68 in the low quartile, yet both have median 27 heavy atoms. Smaller aromatic-ring count and different polar-ring organization correlate with higher labels; this is not evidence of a chemical requirement for N-F. Parent leaders also retain questionable N-halogen or small-ring closure chemistry. Child seed endpoints 0/1/2 are 0.5359220956579449, 0.5822404371063148, 0.487179299011358; published Parent endpoints are 0.6942804632817005, 0.4999004646832901, 0.6201223048692813.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally reported for n-c55c3d520a2c, carried through n-62daf219c70a and the published n-1744a1494180 molecular assessment, and re-observed in n-6ebafca203bf under the current profile, Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 observations including ten initial per objective and matched sulfur-gated Parent. These are conditional output associations; the hybrid residual law, original mean and inherited gate are not separately attributed. Across 4350 generated observations, direct N-halogen presence is Child 938 versus Parent 786 and O-halogen presence 262 versus 217. Sulfur-halogen presence falls from 93 to 8, while N-halogen amides, ring N-F and O-Cl/O-Br alternatives remain among stronger labels. Non-N-halogen amides and near-ceiling aryl amines provide counterexamples to universal dependence on the suspicious attachment.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not reliably preserve conventional local functional-group environments while modifying productive aromatic and heterocyclic arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Represent intact bond environments and offer conventional alternatives retaining relationships learned from accepted task-local feedback. A narrow permitted sulfur signature is not a whole-molecule stability or synthesis certificate. Preserve useful sulfur and other heteroatoms where supported; this evidence neither authorizes weakening the inherited gate nor demonstrates that a broader reactive-bond filter improves endpoints.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally reported for n-c55c3d520a2c, carried through n-62daf219c70a and the published n-1744a1494180 molecular assessment, and re-observed in n-6ebafca203bf under the current profile, Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 observations including ten initial per objective and matched sulfur-gated Parent. These are conditional output associations; the hybrid residual law, original mean and inherited gate are not separately attributed. Leaders include four-membered fused closures, carbon-bridged polycycles, unsaturated connected medium rings and aromatic-labelled nine-membered nitrogen rings. Carbon allenes occur in 148 Child generated observations versus Parent 11; many are acyclic substituents, not all cyclic cumulenes or intrinsically implausible molecules. Some ring-unsaturation flags decline while others increase. Ring richness is already present and is not the missing capability.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently distinguish valence-valid closures from geometrically credible unsaturation and connected-ring topology.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make ring transformations sensitive to size, bond geometry, bridge connectivity and whole-ring conjugation while retaining feasible alternatives with useful chemical relationships. Do not ban small, fused, medium or macrocyclic rings or every allene indiscriminately. Neither aromatic notation nor sulfur containment supplies geometric validation; a causal score benefit from geometry constraints remains untested.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally reported for n-c55c3d520a2c, carried through n-62daf219c70a and the published n-1744a1494180 molecular assessment, and re-observed in n-6ebafca203bf under the current profile, Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 observations including ten initial per objective and matched sulfur-gated Parent. These are conditional output associations; the hybrid residual law, original mean and inherited gate are not separately attributed. All Child and Parent digest stereocentre-string incidences are zero. RDKit perceives unassigned tetrahedral centres in 2015 of 4350 Child generated records versus Parent 2455, especially in aryl cyclic amines and substituted bridged rings. Some leaders are achiral under that perception. Allenes and imine/alkene geometries add configuration questions outside this tetrahedral count.
transferable_gaps.gap: Potentially stereogenic and configurational molecular arrangements remain incompletely specified after generation.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Preserve or resolve stereochemistry where meaningful, and handle achiral, meso and configurationally unstable cases appropriately. Assess tautomerism and protonation separately because neutral notation coexists with useful amines. This is an identity gap rather than evidence that stereo penalties improve scores, and it identifies no component responsible for omission.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally reported for n-c55c3d520a2c, carried through n-62daf219c70a and the published n-1744a1494180 molecular assessment, and re-observed in n-6ebafca203bf under the current profile, Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 observations including ten initial per objective and matched sulfur-gated Parent. These are conditional output associations; the hybrid residual law, original mean and inherited gate are not separately attributed. Child still emits 69 generated observations with at most three heavy atoms versus Parent 82. Floor-scoring fragments coexist with large doubled aromatic amides or polyene elaborations far below their compact family leaders. One emitted connected system reaches 119 heavy atoms. The stronger aryl-amine score stratum has median 28 heavy atoms versus 38 in its lower stratum, whereas several other strata have similar sizes despite large label differences.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator inconsistently retains useful functional-group context during fragmentation, growth and reconnection.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Use accepted task-local feedback to preserve useful combinations of regions during shrinkage, growth and recombination. Allow genuine simplification and productive elaboration. Neither a fixed minimum size nor a generic preference for additional aromatic mass follows from these observations; attribution to a particular operator or guaranteed benefit from size restrictions remains unsupported.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Originally reported for n-c55c3d520a2c, carried through n-62daf219c70a and the published n-1744a1494180 molecular assessment, and re-observed in n-6ebafca203bf under the current profile, Search seeds 0/1/2, 300 observations including ten initial per objective and matched sulfur-gated Parent. These are conditional output associations; the hybrid residual law, original mean and inherited gate are not separately attributed. Leaders within seeds repeatedly vary nitrogen-halogen substitution, short chains, imino/carbonyl groups and adjacent ring segments. Three best-scoring amide variants have the identical evaluator label while changing only ring N-halogen attachment. Different seeds nevertheless reach distinct amide, heterocyclic, aryl-amine and nitrogen/carbonyl families. This is limited local alternatives, not global collapse, and no full-history chemical mediation analysis is supplied.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemically independent plausible alternatives to locally successful scaffold families are inconsistently represented among the leaders.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Offer independent feasible connectivities retaining favorable relationships inferred from current observations, then assess actual accepted labels and chemistry separately. Distinct strings alone do not establish useful molecular coverage. Preserve original gap provenance and source conditions in later catalog use; these associations justify neither objective-specific templates nor guaranteed gains from raising diversity.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
